text:
tanya (eng-sre): Quick proposal — I want to add a composite SLO for the GPU fleet that covers: 99p latency (inference tail), queue saturation (GPU queue depth), and a small availability component (node-level Pod eviction failures). The goal is a single error budget signal for capacity planning and monthly cost forecasts.

michael (eng-platform): +1 on a composite view. How do you imagine weighting latency vs saturation? they can diverge.

tanya (eng-sre): My thinking: 50% latency-tail, 35% saturation, 15% availability. We need latency to capture user-facing regressions, saturation for capacity pressure, and avail for node/network faults. Open to suggestions.

raj (eng-runtime): Two quick concerns: 1) Prometheus cardinality for per-tenant queue metrics if we track per-queue. 2) How we compute 99p for batched inference (requests compressing). We should use request-level observed latency, not per-token.

irina (observability): For cardinality, we can record aggregate per-pool metrics and keep per-tenant only for sampled traces. Example recording rule I'd propose for the queue tail: 

```
# record 99p of GPU queue duration per pool (5m window)
- record: pool:gpu_queue_99p:rate5m
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_gpu_queue_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
```

That keeps cardinality bounded by pool.

michael (eng-platform): Good. Can we also smooth burn rate so short blips don't blow the budget? We had a one-hour spike last month that was noisy.

tanya (eng-sre): Yes — plan is two-pronged: rolling weighted smoothing (EWMA with 3h time constant) for burn rate display + a fallback rule for on-call paging only when sustained for >20m. So dashboards show the smoothed burn, alerts use the raw sustained condition.

irina (observability): Dashboard changes I’ll make: 1) new composite SLO panel (weighted score), 2) burn rate panel with both raw and EWMA overlay, 3) per-pool contribution bar. Also add an annotation stream for rollout events so we can correlate.

raj (eng-runtime): Also flag: GPU queue metric is influenced by batching. We need to normalize by effective concurrency. We should use `redwood_gpu_queue_length / redwood_gpu_effective_slots` as saturation ratio.

irina (observability): Agreed. Proposed alert rule (Prome): 

```
- alert: GPUQueueSaturation
  expr: (sum(redwood_gpu_queue_length) by (pool) / sum(redwood_gpu_effective_slots) by (pool)) > 0.8
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU pool {{ $labels.pool }} saturation > 80% for 15m"
```

We can tune to 10m/15m after some e2e testing.

alertbot: NOTE: On-call rotation will only be paged for `severity=page`. All other notifications go to #eng-sre.

luis (finance): Quick cost question — if we try to keep 99p latency at current levels but add a saturation SLO, are we expecting headroom increases? Rough ballpark impact?

tanya (eng-sre): Short answer: yes, likely ~5–12% additional reserved capacity on high-variance pools unless we change batching or autoscale thresholds. We can offset with smarter prefix caching and cold-start mitigations.

michael (eng-platform): For error budget forecasting, I'd like a simple export (CSV) of the composite burn rate so capacity/planning can run a monthly projection. Can the dashboard export a 30d burn forecast?

irina (observability): I'll add a forecast panel using Holt-Winters with uncertainty band and an export button. Implementation note: forecasting runs in Grafana backend job; it reads the smoothed burn rate_series.

raj (eng-runtime): Ops note — when we roll this out, we need to ship small changes to the exporters: add pool label to `redwood_gpu_effective_slots` and incrementally backfill. Will coordinate with SDK owners.

luis (finance): If we see that 5–12% reserve estimate, we should bake that into Dedicated capacity quotes. I can update the pricing model once we have a pilot.

michael (eng-platform): One more edge-case: cross-region routing. If NYC is saturated, we should automatically failover to SFO lower-cost pool without affecting error budget calculation. We need the SLO math to be region-aware (global composite + per-region).

tanya (eng-sre): Yep — plan: compute both per-region and global composite SLOs. Error budget burn attribution will be tagged with region so we can decide rate-limited failover thresholds.

irina (observability): I'll add `region` to the composite breakdown and a per-region burn heatmap. Also will add an alert mute rule during planned cross-region failovers.

raj (eng-runtime): Implementation timeline?

tanya (eng-sre): Proposal: week 1 — exporters + recording rules and dashboard skeleton; week 2 — forecasting/exports + alert tuning; week 3 — pilot on non-prod pool, week 4 — ramp to prod and roll to other pools.

luis (finance): Sounds good. Ping me when you have pilot numbers.

michael (eng-platform): +1. Please create a short RFC doc with the weighting choices and test plan.

tanya (eng-sre): Will do — I'll drop RFC + Prometheus snippets in the repo and @channel the pilot start. TL;DR: composite SLO + bounded cardinality recording rules + smoothed burn for dashboards + sustained raw alerts for paging.

irina (observability): I'll open a Grafana PR for the dashboard changes and a prometheus-rules PR with the recording & alert rules.

alertbot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window tonight 02:00–03:00 UTC. Dashboards may show transient gaps.

michael (eng-platform): Thanks — also please include a simple regression test harness so we don't accidentally tune away real regressions.

raj (eng-runtime): Noted. I'll add synthetic traffic test for tail latency/pool saturation.

luis (finance): rough acceptance: if pilot shows <10% additional reserved cost and better burn predictability, we roll.

tanya (eng-sre): Great — thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link here once created and schedule a short sync after pilot data. :thumbsup:
